design.model: X=(h1,a1,h2,a2) ~ N(mean, Sigma4). mean=(s_h*mu_home, s_a*mu_away, (1-s_h)*mu_home, (1-s_a)*mu_away) with mu from the frozen incumbent; Sigma4 = walk-forward uncentred second moments of the four residuals. Totals/team totals: normal tail at the half-integer strike. Margins: the zero cell is re-weighted by kappa (first half: walk-forward tie factor; full game: 0, a final cannot be tied) and other cells rescaled; overtime probability = kappa_ot x normal mass of the full-game margin in (-0.5, 0.5). Second-half contracts (Kalshi: overtime included) are the remainder final - first half.
design.not_in_scope: Margin SD calibration (wave-15) and roster centring (wave-16) of the full-game model are other workstreams; the incumbent's mean margin and total are taken as given, including its known early-season total bias.
design.point_in_time: Latest incumbent projection with as_of < scheduled tip; scheduled tip = min(last pre-game ESPN schedule observation, the projection's own listed start). Walk-forward by slate day; a training game must also have had its period score archived before the first tip of the slate (the first three slates therefore run on the prior alone).

priors.source: sd_team 10.38 and rho_home_away 0.32: WAVE13_GAME_NUMBER.md section 4 (the values IMPLIED by the incumbent's frozen margin_sd / total_sd; they depend on no game result, so quoting a report written inside the evaluation window leaks nothing). share_1h 0.47, rho_1h_2h 0, kappa 1.0 and ot_base_rate 0.05 are this slice's structural ASSUMPTIONS (no number in the owner's reports); pseudo-count 30 games (kappa: 3 expected ties).

design.question: Can the incumbent's frozen full-game projection be extended, without touching its means, into one coherent joint distribution that gives calibrated probabilities for first-half, team-total and overtime contracts?
references: naive:independent-halves (uncorrelated team scores, fixed 0.5 share, walk-forward team SD / sqrt(2) per half, no tie calibration)
incumbent:pure-0.2.0 (frozen home_win_prob; Phi((margin-line)/margin_sd); Phi((total-line)/total_sd); full-game families only: it publishes nothing else)

incumbent-shadow:score_distribution(reconstructed) (team totals from the frozen SDs under the incumbent's documented uncorrelated total/margin assumption; reconstructed here, the archive stores no such probability)
design.statistics: Per-row paired loss difference (challenger - reference; negative = challenger better), cluster bootstrap by game_id (2000 draws, seed 7). Cohorts: slates before 2026-11-07 vs from 2026-11-07 (two chronological halves of the date range). 'replicated' = same non-zero sign in pooled and both cohorts. Holm across the headline rows (pooled Brier vs naive, incumbent, incumbent-shadow and market); all other rows carry p_holm = 1.0. Verdict = contract.verdict_from.

universes.all_games: Every used game, outcome-scored on a fixed synthetic ladder: strikes = floor(center)+0.5 + offsets, center from the frozen incumbent mean (first half: 0.47 x mean), offsets (-6,-3,0,3,6) for spreads / team totals / first-half lines and (-8,-4,0,4,8) for the game total; first-half winner = home / away / tie rows; one moneyline row and one overtime row per game.
universes.kalshi_listed: Contracts Kalshi actually listed, at their listed strikes, restricted to rows with a usable mid at the latest pre-tip snapshot.

kalshi_family_inventory.note: Per-game Kalshi series seen in the panel archive. Contracts = distinct tickers. 'used games' = games with a pre-tip incumbent projection and verified half scores.
kalshi_family_inventory.tie_handling: The panel has no rules text field. Tie handling is taken from contract_semantics.yes_condition: KXNCAAMB1H lists three contracts per game (home_wins_1H, away_wins_1H, tied_1H), so a tied half settles both team contracts NO; this is confirmed against Kalshi's settled results (see check own_settlement_matches_kalshi_settled_result).

limitations: 489 games on 12 slate days (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-12): about two weeks of early-season play. Every interval here is wide and no result should be read as settled.
November-only, mostly non-conference schedule with many mismatches; first-half share, half correlations and tie rates may differ in conference play and in March.

The first three slates are forecast from the documented prior alone because no verified period score had been archived before those tips; several prior values (first-half share 0.47, independent halves, continuity factors 1.0) are this slice's assumptions, not owner-published numbers, and they were chosen by the author after the season had started.

The incumbent publishes no probability for first-half, team-total or overtime contracts, so against the incumbent the challenger adds coverage, not accuracy. Accuracy claims are only relative to a naive construction and to the Kalshi mid.

The Kalshi reference is a snapshot mid (two-sided, spread at most 10 cents) from the last capture before tip, typically minutes before tip, while the challenger uses a projection frozen hours earlier. A mid is not an executable fill; no fees, depth or slippage are modelled and nothing here is a betting result.
Kalshi lists first-half spread / total, team-total and overtime contracts for only a small subset of games, so those market comparisons rest on a few dozen games or fewer.
The incumbent's mean total and margin are taken as given, including its documented early-season scoring-level bias; that bias flows into first-half and team-total probabilities.

Scores are modelled with a normal approximation plus a re-weighted zero-margin cell; other key-number effects and skew in blowouts are not modelled. Second-half contracts are priced only as the remainder (final minus first half).
The synthetic all-games ladder is not a set of traded lines; rows inside a game are strongly dependent (handled by the game-cluster bootstrap) and the effective sample is the number of games.
Race-to-N and winning-margin-band contracts are not modelled. The raw Kalshi rules text was not read; contract meaning comes from the panel's parsed semantics.
Archive git history was not audited (depth-1 fetch); the prospective claim rests on in-file freeze timestamps and manifest hashes.

verdict.reason: 21 headline pooled Brier comparisons (Holm-adjusted): 0 VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT, 0 IMPROVED_NOT_VALIDATED, 2 NOT_IMPROVED, 19 INCONCLUSIVE. Favourable: none. Unfavourable: ['game_moneyline vs market:kalshi_mid', 'game_spread vs market:kalshi_mid']. The incumbent publishes no probability for first-half, team-total or overtime contracts, so the challenger's contribution there is COVERAGE with measured calibration, not an accuracy gain over the incumbent; any gain is over a naive construction, on about two weeks of November games, and the overall verdict stays INCONCLUSIVE unless every market-facing comparison is also favourable. The incumbent's full-game probabilities are retained.
